title: Risk-aware cutlist playbook — October 2026
content:
Purpose:
This playbook defines a lightweight, repeatable process for creating a cutlist driven by risk and customer impact rather than only by feature size or team preference. Goal: reduce production exposure and unblock the sprint while preserving user-facing SLAs and rollout safety.

Scope & when to use this doc:
- Use during sprint planning when backlog size exceeds team capacity by >20%.
- Use for emergency triage when incidents threaten SLAs and multiple backlog items are candidates for decommit.
- Applicable to Console and Rollouts verticals: intake workflows, route decision UI, rollout gating, per-route metrics, and rollout/action tools.

Definitions (quick):
- Risk Score: composite integer 0–100 combining severity, exposure, frequency, and mitigation cost. Higher = more urgent to address.
- Cutlist: ordered list of backlog items proposed to be removed or deferred from the next sprint commit.
- Decommit: action to move an item out of the active sprint scope.

Triage rubric (fields to capture on each ticket):
- Jira key / short title
- Customer-exposed? (yes/no)
- Severity (S1-S4; S1 highest)
- Frequency (incidents/week or user-sessions impacted)
- Regression probability (high/medium/low)
- Mitigation effort (est. story points or dev hours)
- Rollout dependency surface (number of routes/teams affected)
- Monitoring/alerting coverage present? (yes/no)

Risk scoring formula (example, tunable):
- Severity weight: 40% (S1=100, S2=60, S3=30, S4=10)
- Exposure weight: 30% (customer-exposed=true => 100, internal-only => 40)
- Frequency weight: 20% (normalize incidents/week -> 0-100)
- Mitigation cost penalty: -10% * (effort in normalized units) up to -30
- Final Risk Score = clamp(0, 100, weighted_sum + mitigation_penalty)

Triage categories and recommended outcomes:
- 75–100: Critical risk — prioritize into sprint if <=20% of sprint capacity; otherwise create hotfix lane + dedicate on-call owner.
- 50–74: High risk — prefer to keep in-sprint if owner available; consider slicing into smaller deliverables and ship mitigation first.
- 25–49: Medium risk — candidate for decommit if sprint is over-subscribed; keep in backlog with monitoring task.
- 0–24: Low risk — defer to next grooming cycle; batch for next planning window.

Example applications (5 tickets assessed during 2026-10-08 grooming):
- RBW-1423: "Route fallback sometimes returns empty response" — customer-exposed: yes; severity S2; freq ~3/day; mitigation 8sp; deps 4 routes; monitoring: partial. Calculated score: 82 => Critical risk. Decision: keep in sprint, pair with canary and rollback plan.
- RBW-1478: "Console filter mis-sort in large org mode" — customer-exposed: yes; severity S3; freq ~2/week; mitigation 5sp; deps 1 route; monitoring: yes. Score: 48 => Medium risk. Decision: decommit if capacity constrained; create smaller follow-up for UX patch.
- RBW-1534: "Telemetry pipeline lag on high-volume tenants" — internal-only; severity S2; freq variable (spikes); mitigation 13sp; deps 3 services; monitoring: yes. Score: 61 => High risk. Decision: split into short-term mitigation (alerts + throttling) in sprint, larger fix in later sprint.
- RBW-1601: "Docs: missing rollout docs for canary API" — customer-exposed: no; severity S4; freq low; mitigation 2sp; score: 18 => Low risk. Decision: defer.
- RBW-1625: "SDK: streaming disconnects on prolonged idle" — customer-exposed: yes; severity S1; freq rare but high impact; mitigation 20sp; monitoring: partial. Score: 70 (High risk) => schedule as WIP with prioritized QA; plan fallback routing.

Wireframe & UX callouts (for Console backlog view):
- Add 'Risk' column with color band: red (>75), orange (50–74), yellow (25–49), grey (<25). Hover shows the rubric breakdown and last incident link.
- Quick actions on ticket row: "Decommit", "Mitigate-first" (create 1sp mitigation subtask), "Escalate to SRE". Each quick action opens a small modal to record rationale and owner.
- Sprint capacity bar should show "% capacity reserved for critical remediation" (recommended default 15%). Allow PM to override with justification log.
- In intake modal, require minimal risk fields: customer-exposed, severity, estimated effort. This nudges submitters to provide signal for later triage.

Cutlist governance rules (must-have):
- Any decommit must be documented with rationale and a link to a Jira comment by the PM or tech lead.
- If more than 3 Critical items exist, create hotfix lane and reduce new feature intake by 50% that sprint.
- No deletion of tickets without owner approval; use decommit status.
- Security-related items (marked by Security tag) cannot be decommitted — escalate to security lead.

Meeting notes (2026-10-08 grooming session):
Attendees: Maya Thompson (PM), Evan Park (Eng lead), Lina Ortega (UX), Samir Patel (SRE), Priya Nair (QA)
Decisions:
- Adopted Risk Score formula above for Q4 grooming trials.
- Reserve 15% sprint capacity for remediation unless leadership signs off.
- RBW-1423 moved to sprint with canary; RBW-1478 decommitted to grooming backlog.
Action items:
- Evan: implement quick-action scaffolding in backlog list (ETA 2026-10-20).
- Lina: wireframe the risk hovercard and capacity bar mockups (ETA 2026-10-15).
- Samir: prepare runbook template for hotfix lane and link to monitoring alerts (ETA 2026-10-14).
- Priya: define minimal QA checklist for mitigation-first tasks (ETA 2026-10-18).
- Maya: update sprint plan and notify stakeholders; add decommit rationale to RBW-1478 (ETA 2026-10-09).

Sprint planning guidance (practical):
- Start with committed features + critical risk items. If total exceeds capacity, run the cutlist: sort candidate items by Risk Score then by dependencies. Decommit from bottom up until capacity met.
- For items with similar scores: prefer decommitting items with high mitigation cost and low customer exposure.
- Maintain a single file (Confluence + linked JSON in Drive) that records cutlist decisions for audit.

Example template for decommit comment (copy into Jira reply):
- Reason: (short)
- Risk Score: (value)
- Owner: (name)
- Action: Decommit / Mitigate-first / Hotfix lane
- Planned revisit date: YYYY-MM-DD
- Link to follow-up ticket(s): (if split)

Notes on iteration and tuning:
- Re-run weights monthly for the first quarter of adoption. Prefer to track false positives (items scored high but not acted on) and false negatives (items low score but produce incidents) and adjust weights accordingly.
- Instrument backlog UI interactions to gather friction metrics: time to decommit, number of quick action uses, and required overrides.

Appendix: sample short-term rollout for RBW-1423 (operational checklist)
- Create canary rule for the affected route (Dev): Evan (2026-10-09)
- Add temporary prefix fallback to stable model (Dev): Samir (2026-10-10)
- Postmortem template (owner): Maya (complete within 3 business days after fix)

Open questions & known gaps:
- How to handle cross-team items that have different severity perceptions? Proposal: require an alignment comment from each impacted team lead for items scoring >75.
- Should we include cost-savings as a negative risk factor (i.e., low-cost optimizations deprioritized)? Hold for v2.

Next steps (immediate):
1) Finalize wireframes and hand to frontend for quick-actions (owner: Lina + Evan).
2) Add the scoring fields to the intake template and automate Risk Score calculation in backlog view (owner: Maya + Eng infra).
3) Run two trial sprints (Oct and Nov) with the new process and collect metrics on decommit frequency and incident delta.

If you have feedback or need different examples added to the doc, drop notes here or ping me in #product-console.

-- Maya
